Lucrative

LOO-kruh-tiv — starts like 'loot'; a lucrative deal brings in plenty of loot. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Lucrative is producing a great deal of profit.

The small startup signed an unexpectedly lucrative contract that tripled its yearly revenue overnight.

Worked Example

A teenager starts mowing lawns for five dollars each over the summer. Within two years, word spreads, he hires three friends to help, buys better equipment, and now runs a small business that earns him more in a summer than most part-time jobs pay in a year.

Growing into something that earns real, substantial profit is exactly what makes a business lucrative. Unlike 'busy,' which just means a lot of activity, lucrative specifically means highly profitable.

How Lucrative Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

profitable

profitable: producing financial gain

rewarding

rewarding: providing satisfaction or gain, often financial

lucrative

lucrative: highly profitable (itself the target word's own root sense)

Antonyms

unprofitable

unprofitable: not producing any financial gain

worthless

worthless: having no financial or practical value

How Strong Is It? — profitable → lucrative → booming

profitable vs. lucrative

profitable vs. lucrative: Profitable is a milder, more general word than lucrative — something profitable simply earns money, while lucrative implies the profit is especially large or impressive.

booming vs. lucrative

booming vs. lucrative: Booming can feel even bigger than lucrative: lucrative describes strong, steady profit, but booming suggests rapid, explosive growth on top of that profit.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — lucr-

root — lucr-: profit, gain (Latin (lucrum))

suffix — -ative

suffix — -ative: tending to, having the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin lucrum meant 'profit, gain.' Something lucrative, at its root, has a strong tendency to produce exactly that — real financial gain.

Use the root in a new word: lucre

Use the root in a new word: lucre: The pirates argued for hours over how to split their ill-gotten lucre.
